label: ndcgtree16test
authorisation: author-authorised single test look, 2026-08-12: 'add 16th step, run on test. we are changing comparator, we are NOT changing this tree'
comparator_note: THE POLICY-A-SELECTED COMPARATOR. This is the `combined` arm of greedy_static_i26c.json, whose ORDER was selected under the retired policy-A candidate mask (docs/results/MASK_POLICY_B_MIGRATION.md records its intercept_eval 0.13139/0.02343 as the policy-A bridge; policy B is 0.15855/0.02819). Its SEQUENCE is re-scored in-run under policy B here, so the comparison is question-for-question at equal K -- but because its order was CHOSEN on a different ruler, the K=1 difference carries a selection-protocol offset (+0.00093 full on validation) that is NOT conditioning and that sits inside every K>=2 number. The clean policy-B comparator is paused mid-rebuild with 7 of 16 picks banked. DO NOT quote these gains as if that rebuild had happened.
policyB_comparator_status: PAUSED mid-rebuild with 7 of 16 picks banked in ndcgtree16_heaps/greedy_static_policyB_combined_heap.json; resumes after this look.
negative_leaf_note: A NEGATIVE leaf is a RESULT, not a bug. A leaf must carry its ancestors' questions, which were chosen for its PARENTS' cohorts, so the static order is NOT inside a leaf's search space and a leaf can legitimately score below it.
absolute_reporting_note: Absolute cohort-weighted NDCG@10 is reported for BOTH arms at every K, alongside the m=0 intercept (what a user gets for answering nothing). The author intends to read these against the current static ON THE EXPLICIT ASSUMPTION THAT IT IS WEAK, because its order was selected under policy A. Absolutes make that assumption inspectable: if the tree's absolute sits close to the static's, a weak comparator cannot be hiding much; if it is far above, the comparator's weakness matters more. Differences alone do not let a reader make that judgement, which is why the intercept is included -- it is the first time it has been printed for the test cohort.

size_vs_gain.interpretation: On validation the relationship was Spearman -0.55 (p=0.035): small leaves gained most, which is the overfitting signature the genre experiment was built to detect. Whether it PERSISTS on test is what decides how much of the validation gain is real. A negative rho surviving to test would mean the small leaves are genuinely better served; a rho that goes to zero or flips means the validation pattern was fitted noise.
